NVD Fresh Produce Pty Ltd
Walkaway, Western Australia

Full Time Agriculture Technician 
(2 Positions Available)

Salary
AUD $95,000 – $110,000 per annum plus Superannuation, depending on skills and experience.

About us:
NVD Fresh Produce Pty Ltd is a family-owned agricultural enterprise based in Walkaway, Western Australia, approximately 30 minutes from Geraldton. We operate approximately 4.2 hectares of plastic greenhouses in Walkaway and an additional 2 hectares of plastic greenhouses at the family’s original farm.

We are currently expanding our operations, having purchased 60 acres of land near Walkaway to support future growth and long-term sustainability. NVD Fresh Produce specialises in intensive greenhouse cultivation and is progressively diversifying its crop range, recognising crop rotation as a key strategy to preserve soil health, improve productivity, and maintain consistent supply.

The business is focused on strengthening its production capacity, improving operational systems and water management practices, and establishing a scalable and sustainable structure to support ongoing expansion within Western Australia’s fresh produce market.

The successful applicant will play an important role in supporting the continued growth and success of NVD Fresh Produce's farming operations.

Position Summary
The Agriculture Technician is responsible for maintaining, diagnosing and repairing agricultural vehicles, machinery and equipment used in NVD Fresh Produce's farming operations. The role supports efficient farm operations by ensuring agricultural machinery is maintained in a safe, reliable and operational condition.

Key Responsibilities
Agricultural Machinery Maintenance
•	Diagnose faults in diesel engines, transmissions and mechanical components. 
•	Carry out repairs and maintenance on tractors, trucks, harvesters and other agricultural machinery. 
•	Perform scheduled servicing to maximise equipment reliability. 
•	Test machinery to ensure safe and efficient operation. 
Farm Equipment Support
•	Undertake on-site repairs across farm operations. 
•	Maintain maintenance records and report equipment issues. 
•	Order and monitor spare parts and workshop consumables. 
•	Assist in minimising machinery downtime during production periods. 
Workplace Safety
•	Follow workplace health and safety procedures. 
•	Maintain a clean and safe workshop environment. 
•	Work collaboratively with farm managers and other employees.

Qualifications and Skills
Applicants should demonstrate:
•	Relevant trade qualification in diesel mechanics, agricultural mechanics, automotive mechanics or a related field will be highly regarded. 
•	At least 1 year's relevant experience in the maintenance and repair of agricultural machinery and diesel-powered equipment is required.
•	Ability to diagnose, repair and maintain agricultural machinery and equipment efficiently. 
•	Ability to read and interpret technical manuals, maintenance procedures and equipment specifications. 
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively as part of a team. 
•	Current driver's licence or the ability to obtain one will be highly regarded. 
•	Commitment to workplace health and safety.


How to apply:

Applications open on 10 July 2026 and close on 9 August 2026
Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.

We have an exciting opportunity for an IT Operations Engineer to join our National Operations Centre (NOC) team. We are seeking candidates with a strong background in IT systems and networks, coupled with extensive experience in managing IT service desk operations, and providing high-level support to internal and external staff. In this role, you will play a pivotal part in collaborating with various IT teams, ensuring the delivery of high-quality services to the business, while striving for operational excellence.

Please note this will be a permanent, full-time role based out of our Sydney CBD Office. It will involve participation in a continuous shift roster - working 4 days on and 4 days off. The shift patterns will be made up of 2-day shifts from 7am-7pm and 2-night shifts from 7pm-7am. 

Some of your responsibilities will include and are not limited to
•	Monitoring critical business services and systems, networks and infrastructure
•	Provide after-hours service desk support to users
•	Identify and address issues before they affect business operations
•	Handle and administer privileged accounts securely

What you’ll have done
•	Seasoned service desk analyst, NOC or equivalent experience (minimum 2 years), ideally in a continuous shift operations centre (24/7x365)
•	Strong technical knowledge of networking protocols such as TCP/IP, SNMP, DNS, DHCP, and other networking protocols
•	Strong problem-solving skills to identify and resolve issues quickly, including experience with major incidents
•	Familiarity with server operating systems (e.g., Windows, Linux) and basic server administration
•	Experience with technology service monitoring tools - systems, application, and networks such as Centreon, Solarwinds, PTRG desirable
•	Familiarity with IT service management tools and frameworks (ITIL v3/4)
•	Demonstrated experience in delivering exemplary support, customer service and training
•	Excellent documentation skills for keeping records of issues, resolutions, and operational procedures
•	Effective communication with the ability to work as part of a team, especially in a high-pressure environment where collaboration is essential to solving issues

What we can offer you
•	5 weeks annual leave 
•	Annual salary between 90,000 - 95,000
•	Opportunities to progress within I-MED’s continued growth and expansion 
•	Being part of a team that makes a difference to the functioning of our ever-growing business 
•	Experience in communicating with different areas of IT 
•	Enjoy exclusive benefits including discounted private health insurance, salary packaging, Fitness Passport access, lifestyle and travel discounts, I-MED services for your family and employee wellbeing support.

About Us
At I-MED, we're more than just a medical imaging provider - we're a community of passionate professionals committed to excellence for our patients. With over 200 clinics and a staggering 6 million patient procedures annually, we proudly stand as one of the largest providers of medical imaging in the world. Our success lies in our people with over 350 dedicated doctors and 4,000 staff members who actively share clinical knowledge and expertise. 

If you're looking for the next step in your career and are passionate about the delivery of excellence within healthcare services, apply today!

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









About the Role 






Monash Biochemistry Laboratory is seeking enthusiastic and motivated Medical Laboratory Scientists to join our dynamic and highly skilled team. Multiple positions are available, with consideration given to both full-time and part-time appointments.






As a 24-7 diagnostic laboratory, we provide routine and acute biochemistry testing services that support patient care across a diverse clinical setting. Successful applicants will have the opportunity to work with a broad range of analytical platforms and specialised testing services in a fast-paced and collaborative environment. The successful applicant will contribute to the delivery of high-quality diagnostic testing, including: 









Routine and urgent biochemistry testing 












Quality assurance and quality control activities 












Instrument maintenance and troubleshooting 












Result validation and interpretation 












Participation in a rotating roster, including evenings, nights, weekends and public holidays as required 












Specialised testing, including protein electrophoresis and mass spectrometry (where applicable) 















Essential Criteria:









Bachelor of Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or equivalent qualification recognised by AIMS or the AACB. 












Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a fast-paced laboratory environment. 












Ability to maintain accuracy and attention to detail while working under pressure. 












Strong organisational, communication and teamwork skills. 












Commitment to providing a high-quality diagnostic service. 















Desirable Criteria:









Previous experience working in a diagnostic Biochemistry laboratory. 












Experience performing and interpreting serum and urine protein electrophoresis. 












Experience in mass spectrometry, including method development, validation and troubleshooting. 












Experience working within a NATA-accredited laboratory environment. 












Familiarity with laboratory information systems and automated chemistry analysers.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Kevin Jessen, on (03) 9594 2055.

Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.

# Motor Mechanic

## About Gold Coast Car Electrics & Mechanical

Gold Coast Car Electrics & Mechanical is a trusted independent automotive workshop committed to delivering high-quality mechanical repairs, servicing and diagnostic solutions. We service a wide range of petrol, diesel and hybrid vehicles, combining advanced diagnostic technology with skilled workmanship to ensure our customers' vehicles remain safe, reliable and performing at their best.

We are seeking a qualified and motivated **Motor Mechanic** to join our growing team. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who takes pride in their workmanship, enjoys solving technical problems and values delivering outstanding customer service.

## Key Responsibilities

As a Motor Mechanic, you will be responsible for:

* Diagnosing mechanical faults using diagnostic equipment and technical expertise.
* Performing servicing, maintenance and repairs on petrol, diesel and hybrid vehicles in accordance with manufacturer specifications.
* Inspecting engines, transmissions, suspension, steering, braking and cooling systems to identify faults and determine repair requirements.
* Removing, dismantling, repairing and replacing worn or defective mechanical components.
* Carrying out engine tuning, timing adjustments and performance-related repairs to ensure optimum vehicle operation.
* Inspecting and repairing driveline components, clutches, gearboxes, differentials and exhaust systems.
* Completing scheduled logbook servicing, preventative maintenance and vehicle safety inspections.
* Testing vehicles before and after repairs to verify that faults have been rectified and the vehicle is safe and roadworthy.
* Maintaining accurate service records and clearly communicating repair recommendations to customers and the service team.
* Ensuring all work is completed efficiently while complying with workplace health and safety requirements and industry standards.
* Maintaining a clean, organised and safe workshop environment, including the proper care of tools and equipment.

## Essential Qualifications and Experience

* AQF Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology (or equivalent) with at least two years of on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV. Alternatively, a minimum of three years of relevant industry experience.
* At least two years' experience as a qualified Motor Mechanic is preferred.
* Current Australian driver's licence (preferred).

## Skills and Attributes

The successful applicant will demonstrate:

* Strong diagnostic and fault-finding skills across a wide range of vehicle makes and models.
* Sound knowledge of automotive mechanical systems and manufacturer repair procedures.
* Experience using modern diagnostic scan tools and workshop equipment.
* Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.
* Strong customer service and communication skills.
* Good organisational and time-management skills with the ability to prioritise workloads.
* The ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
* A strong commitment to quality workmanship, workplace safety and customer satisfaction.

## Employment Details

* **Position:** Permanent Full-Time
* **Salary:** AU$80,000 per annum plus employer superannuation contributions at the statutory rate.
* **Location:** Ashmore, Gold Coast, Queensland
* **Job Type:** Full-time

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Permanent Part Time
Position Classification: Enrolled Nurse
Remuneration: 75011.91 - 81508.14 full-time equivalent base salary range (+12% super + 17.5% leave loading and salary packaging) 
Hours Per Week: 22
Requisition ID: REQ676835
Located in: Westmead
Applications Close: Midnight on 19 July 2026
For role related queries or questions contact Melanie Wong on melanie.wong@health.nsw.gov.au
 

At the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, every role helps children and young people live their healthiest lives.

As the largest paediatric health service in Australia, we care for thousands of children each year, in hospital and at home. Our people are united by compassion, collaboration and excellence in care.

The Allergy and Immunology Service is seeking an enthusiastic enrolled nurse with experience in allergy skin testing and food challenges, or a willingness to undertake training to do so, to work in supervised multidisciplinary outpatient and inpatient settings. Experience working with children and families in a medical setting is essential.

What you'll be doing
 

The enrolled nurse will work under the supervision of the registered nurse and is responsible for delivering allergy diagnostic services -with an emphasis on allergy skin testing and comprehensive nursing care to patients and their families, demonstrating and applying knowledge in all aspects of care including collaborating with physicians and multidisciplinary team members to provide nursing care to allergy patients in the outpatient and inpatient setting; taking appropriate clinical measurements relative to the patient's condition; conducting allergy skin testing, assisting with allergy food challenge clinics, providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends, and families; maintaining an empathetic approach to families. 
 

Additional Benefits (where applicable): Flexible work opportunities, Salary packaging and meal entertainment benefits, accrued days off (ADOs), fitness passport, employee assistance program (EAP)

How to Apply:
Click 'Apply Online' and submit your application including:

A resume (maximum 5 pages) outlining your experience 

Responses to the questions below:

Experience with allergy skin testing- or a willingness to undertake training in allergy skin testing.

Experience with working with children and families in a medical setting.

Current registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA) as an Enrolled Nurse.

Demonstrated excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills.

Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team.

Demonstrated ability to effectively prioritise and organise own workload.

Demonstrates commitment to working effectively within a team to provide quality nursing services.

 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 

Child Safe Standards:
SCHN is committed to maintaining a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, in line with NSW Health's commitment to the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

Additional Information: 

SCHN is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity, recognising that a diverse workforce strengthens our culture and enhances the care we provide to children, young people and their families.

Permanent NSW Health roles require Australian citizenship or permanent residency. Temporary visa holders may be considered where no suitable Australian citizen or permanent resident is identified.

NSW Health vaccination and screening requirements must be met prior to commencement. 

This position requires a Working with Children Check (WWCC) issued by the Office of the Children's Guardian.

Where required, overseas qualifications must be formally assessed by the Department of Education or relevant authority for recognition in Australia.

An Eligibility List may be created for future permanent and temporary part time vacancies. 

Need more information? 
 1) Click here for the Position Description
 2) Find out more about applying for this position

 

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are strongly encouraged to apply. We recognise the value of Aboriginal staff providing health care to Aboriginal children and families. For application support, visit the NSW Health Aboriginal Recruitment tool, Stepping Up to assist in preparing your application, or contact the SCHN's Aboriginal Workforce Consultant at SCHN-EA-AboriginalHealthDirectorate@health.nsw.gov.au

For technical support please contact 1300 679 367

Learn more about The Sydney Children's Hospitals Network

result.description:
Gilmac, Australia's top hay exporter, handles a quarter of the country's hay exports across three states, with major markets in Japan, Korea, and Taiwan.

 

We are seeking a qualified Electrician to support our hay processing plant operations, based out of our Midvale workshop travelling regionally to sites in Wagin, York and New Norcia to support routine weekly preventative maintenance while also contributing during planned shutdown maintenance and other plant upgrades. 

 

Responsibilities

Schedule and perform routine electrical maintenance on automated hay press, conveyors, strapping equipment, packaging machinery and associated plant systems.

Diagnose and repair electrical faults on fixed plant, motors, sensors, control panels, drives and ancillary equipment.

Assist with breakdown response, planned shutdowns and preventative maintenance across site equipment.

Support troubleshooting of PLC-controlled plant and coordinate contractor support where required.

Maintain electrical records, maintenance database updates and action registers.

Manage stock levels for electrical parts and critical spares.

Work with site and maintenance teams to improve plant uptime, safety, quality and continuous improvement outcomes.

Ensure all electrical work is completed safely and in accordance with Gilmac procedures, isolation requirements and relevant standards.

 

Skills & Experience:

Australian electrical trade qualification and relevant electrical licence/registration.

Experience in industrial, manufacturing, agricultural, processing or fixed plant environments.

Fault finding and maintenance experience across motors, sensors, conveyors, control systems, drives and automated machinery.

PLC, instrumentation, automation or packaging equipment experience would be highly regarded.

Ability to read electrical drawings and apply safe isolation and testing practices.

 

Requirements

Full-time availability and flexibility for after-hours callouts if needed.

Commitment to safety, quality, preventative maintenance and reliable plant operation.

Willingness to learn Gilmac plant systems and support practical improvements across our sites.

Ability to work independently or in a small team.

Current driver’s licence.

Pass pre-employment physical and medical tests, including alcohol and drug screening.



Remuneration: 

Salary package $130,000-$140,000 dependent on experience

To apply send resume to hr@gilmac.com.au
